# Incident Report: Malware Infection — DESKTOP-RNVO9AT (172.17.0.99)

**Evidence reviewed:** `2024-09-04-traffic-analysis-exercise.pcap` (5,091 frames, 2024-09-04 17:32–18:32 UTC), `2024-09-04-traffic-analysis-exercise-alerts.txt` (Suricata/ET alert log), alert screenshot.

## Victim Host

| Attribute | Value | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| IPv4 | **172.17.0.99** | Consistent source of all malicious traffic |
| MAC address | **18:3d:a2:b6:8d:c4** | ARP replies for 172.17.0.99 |
| Windows hostname | **DESKTOP-RNVO9AT** | DHCP Option 12 (frames 1, 3); confirmed via NBNS name registration (`DESKTOP-RNVO9AT<00>`, `<20>`) |
| AD domain | BEPOSITIVE.COM (DC = WIN-CTL9XBQ9Y19, 172.17.0.17) | DNS SRV lookups for `_ldap._tcp...bepositive.com`; NBNS registration `WIN-CTL9XBQ9Y19` |
| Logged-in user | **afletcher** | Kerberos AS-REQ/TGS-REQ exchanges between 172.17.0.99 and DC 172.17.0.17, `CNameString = afletcher`, `realm = BEPOSITIVE.COM` |

## Malware Family

**Win32/Koi Stealer** — **signature-confirmed**, not behavioral inference.

The Suricata alert log fired: `ETPRO TROJAN Win32/Koi Stealer CnC Checkin (POST) M2` (48 hits, first seen 17:35 UTC, src 172.17.0.99 → dst 79.124.78.197:80). Packet inspection of the matching stream confirms the signature is accurate: repeated `POST /foots.php` requests using `Content-Type: application/octet-stream` / `Content-Encoding: binary` with a pipe-delimited body of the form:

```
101|30168213-3be0-a751-81a0-cf3b228c8654|5LHtVruc|f3f3oMg2lz4XGyHy0LidzFiNvSftke//k+COyrO9aBI=
102|30168213-3be0-a751-81a0-cf3b228c8654
```

— a stable bot/victim GUID (`30168213-3be0-a751-81a0-cf3b228c8654`) followed by short-key/encrypted-blob check-in and heartbeat messages, ~50 beacons over the capture window, matching the documented Koi Stealer checkin pattern.

## Indicators of Compromise

**Command-and-control:**
- `79.124.78.197:80` (HTTP, plaintext IP — no domain name was used to reach it; the `Host` header is the literal IP address)

**Malicious URLs / URIs observed:**
- `http://79.124.78.197/foots.php` — primary stealer beacon/exfil POST endpoint (~50 requests, User-Agent spoofed as `Mozilla/4.0 (compatible; MSIE 7.0; Windows NT 10.0; ...)`)
- `http://79.124.78.197/index.php?id=&subid=qIOuKk7U` — secondary gate/tracking endpoint; response contained a token/subid/URL tuple (`HckDcK0czXjaq48jVHNn|qIOuKk7U|http://79.124.78.197/index.php|`), followed by an encrypted POST to `/index.php`. Consistent with pay-per-install/affiliate-tracked loader infrastructure on the same host.

**Malicious domains:** None. All C2 traffic used the raw IP `79.124.78.197`; no DNS resolution for this host was observed in the capture, so no malicious domain can be grounded in the evidence.

**Transferred files / hashes:** None recoverable. All POST bodies to `79.124.78.197` are `application/octet-stream` (encrypted/encoded), and HTTP object export from the full capture shows no executable, archive, or document delivered in the clear over HTTP. Consequently no file name or SHA256 hash can be grounded in this traffic. The initial delivery/dropper mechanism is not observable within this capture window — beaconing to the C2 begins at frame 1668 (17:35 UTC) with no preceding executable download visible.

## Alerts reviewed and assessed non-relevant

The alert log also shows GPL signatures for SMBv1 (`SMB_COM_TRANSACTION Max Data Count of 0`, `NTLMSSP unicode asn1 overflow attempt`, IPC$ access) and an RPC Kerberos-principal-overflow signature, all between 172.17.0.99 and the domain controller 172.17.0.17 at 17:33–17:34 UTC. Packet-level inspection of this stream (tcp.stream 4, port 139) shows only standard SMBv1 Negotiate/Session-Setup/Tree-Connect/Transaction/Logoff commands consistent with routine NetBIOS browser-election and domain traffic — these are known false-positive-prone legacy GPL rules, not evidence of exploitation, and are unrelated to the Koi Stealer compromise.

## Summary

Windows workstation **DESKTOP-RNVO9AT** (172.17.0.99, MAC 18:3d:a2:b6:8d:c4), logged in as domain user **afletcher** (BEPOSITIVE.COM), is infected with **Win32/Koi Stealer** (signature-confirmed). The malware beacons to **79.124.78.197:80** via `/foots.php` and `/index.php`, identifying the host with bot ID `30168213-3be0-a751-81a0-cf3b228c8654`. No malicious domain, downloaded file, or recoverable hash is present in this capture; recommend isolating the host, resetting the `afletcher` credentials, and blocking `79.124.78.197` at the perimeter.
